---
title: Ignore Set-Cookie or query string parameters when caching content on CDN servers
sidebarTitle: Ignore Set-Cookie or query strings
ai-navigation: Configure query string and Set-Cookie cache behavior on a CDN resource via the Customer Portal, REST API, or Terraform.
---

import { MethodSwitch, MethodSection } from "/snippets/method-switch.jsx";

<MethodSwitch>
  <MethodSection id="portal" label="Customer Portal">

<p>The **Ignore query string** and **Ignore Set-Cookie** options control how query parameters and `Set-Cookie` response headers affect CDN caching. Both are available in the **Cache** section of CDN resource settings.</p>

## Query string setting

<p>The **Ignore query string** option determines how the CDN caches URLs that have query parameters. Query parameters are optional key-value pairs separated by `=` and joined by `&`, appearing at the end of a URL after a `?`:</p>

```
http://cdn.example.com/photo.jpeg?id=6&color=blue
```

<p>When disabled, the full query string is included in the cache key, so URLs with different query parameter values are cached as separate objects.</p>

<p>To enable it in the [Gcore Customer Portal](https://portal.gcore.com):</p>

<p>1. In the left sidebar, navigate to **CDN** > **CDN resources** and click the CNAME of the resource to configure.</p>

<Frame>![CDN resources list](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/ignore-the-set-cookie-or-query-string-parameters-when-caching-content-on-cdn-servers/ignore-query-string-image1.png)</Frame>

<p>2. In the sidebar, under **Cache**, click **Query string**.</p>

<Frame>![Resource settings — Query string section in the Cache group](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/ignore-the-set-cookie-or-query-string-parameters-when-caching-content-on-cdn-servers/ignore-query-string-image2.png)</Frame>

<p>3. Enable the **Ignore query string** toggle.</p>

<p>4. Select a mode and set its parameters.</p>

<p>The enabled option has three modes:</p>

| Mode | Parameters in the list | Other parameters |
|------|------------------------|-----------------|
| Ignore all | — | Ignored |
| Ignore all except | Included in cache key | Ignored |
| Ignore only | Ignored | Included in cache key |

- **Ignore all** (default). Files with different query parameters are cached as a single object, regardless of parameter values.

<Frame>![Ignore all mode selected](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/ignore-the-set-cookie-or-query-string-parameters-when-caching-content-on-cdn-servers/ignore-query-string-image3.png)</Frame>

  These URLs are cached as a single object because all parameters are ignored:

  ```
  http://cdn.example.com/photo.jpeg?id=6&color=blue
  http://cdn.example.com/photo.jpeg?id=1&color=blue
  ```

- **Ignore all except**. Files with the specified query parameters are cached as separate objects; files with other parameters are cached as a single object.

  Enter each parameter name on a separate line in the text field that appears.

<Frame>![Ignore all except mode with parameter text field](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/ignore-the-set-cookie-or-query-string-parameters-when-caching-content-on-cdn-servers/ignore-query-string-image4.png)</Frame>

  With `id` in the text field, these URLs are cached as separate objects because the `id` values differ, and the `color` parameter is ignored:

  ```
  http://cdn.example.com/photo.jpeg?id=6&color=blue
  http://cdn.example.com/photo.jpeg?id=1&color=blue
  ```

  With `color` in the text field, these URLs are cached as a single object because the `color` values are the same, and the `id` parameter is ignored:

  ```
  http://cdn.example.com/photo.jpeg?id=6&color=blue
  http://cdn.example.com/photo.jpeg?id=1&color=blue
  ```

- **Ignore only**. Files with the specified query parameters are cached as a single object; files with other parameters are cached as separate objects.

  Enter each parameter name on a separate line in the text field that appears.

<Frame>![Ignore only mode with parameter text field](/images/docs/cdn/cdn-resource-options/cache/ignore-the-set-cookie-or-query-string-parameters-when-caching-content-on-cdn-servers/ignore-query-string-image5.png)</Frame>

  With `id` in the text field, these URLs are cached as a single object because the `id` values are ignored, and the `color` values are the same:

  ```
  http://cdn.example.com/photo.jpeg?id=6&color=blue
  http://cdn.example.com/photo.jpeg?id=1&color=blue
  ```

  With `color` in the text field, these URLs are cached as separate objects because the `color` values are ignored, and the `id` values differ:

  ```
  http://cdn.example.com/photo.jpeg?id=6&color=blue
  http://cdn.example.com/photo.jpeg?id=1&color=blue
  ```

<Warning>Enabling or changing this option may invalidate cached content for URLs with query strings. CDN servers will request those files from the origin again, which can increase origin load.</Warning>

<p>5. Click **Save changes**.</p>

## Set-Cookie setting

<p>When **Ignore Set-Cookie** is disabled, the CDN takes the `Set-Cookie` response header into account when storing the response in cache. Files with different `Set-Cookie` header values are cached as separate objects, so multiple cached copies of the same content can accumulate and the cache hit ratio drops.</p>

<p>The **Ignore Set-Cookie** option changes this behavior: files are cached as a single object regardless of the `Set-Cookie` header value. Gcore recommends enabling this option for the best cache hit ratio.</p>

<p>To enable it, open **Cache** > **Set-Cookie**, enable the **Ignore Set-Cookie** toggle, and click **Save changes**.</p>

</MethodSection>
  <MethodSection id="api" label="REST API">

<p>Update the resource options to control how query parameters and `Set-Cookie` headers affect the CDN cache key. Find the resource ID in [list&nbsp;CDN&nbsp;resources](/api-reference/cdn/cdn-resources/list-cdn-resources).</p>

<Info>
An [API&nbsp;token](/account-settings/api-tokens) is required.
</Info>

```bash
export GCORE_API_KEY="{YOUR_API_KEY}"
export CDN_RESOURCE_ID="{YOUR_RESOURCE_ID}"
```

## Query string

<p>Only one of these three options can be enabled. Enabling a second one returns HTTP 400, so set `enabled` to false on the active option in the same request and keep its `value`.</p>

<p>The samples below switch modes in sequence: Ignore all, then Ignore all except, then Ignore only, then the full query string. When a different query-string option is already enabled, set that option to `enabled` false in the same request.</p>

<p>`value` is required. For `query_params_whitelist` and `query_params_blacklist`, an empty `value` list returns HTTP 400 while the option is enabled.</p>

### Ignore all

<p>Send `ignoreQueryString` with `enabled` true and `value` true. URLs that differ only by query parameters are cached as one object.</p>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Python SDK">
    ```python
    import os
    from gcore import Gcore

    client = Gcore()

    resource = client.cdn.cdn_resources.update(
        int(os.environ["CDN_RESOURCE_ID"]),
        options={
            "ignore_query_string": {"enabled": True, "value": True},
        },
    )
    print(resource.options.ignore_query_string.enabled, resource.options.ignore_query_string.value)
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go SDK">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "strconv"

        gcore "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go"
        "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go/cdn"
    )

    func main() {
        client := gcore.NewClient()
        ctx := context.Background()
        resourceID, err := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("CDN_RESOURCE_ID"), 10, 64)
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }

        resource, err := client.CDN.CDNResources.Update(ctx, resourceID, cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParams{
            Options: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptions{
                IgnoreQueryString: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptionsIgnoreQueryString{
                    Enabled: true,
                    Value:   true,
                },
            },
        })
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }
        fmt.Println(resource.Options.IgnoreQueryString.Enabled, resource.Options.IgnoreQueryString.Value)
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="curl">
    ```bash
    curl -X PATCH "https://api.gcore.com/cdn/resources/$CDN_RESOURCE_ID" \
      -H "Authorization: APIKey $GCORE_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "options": {
          "ignoreQueryString": {
            "enabled": true,
            "value": true
          }
        }
      }'
    ```

    <p>The API returns HTTP 200:</p>

    ```json
    {
      "id": 12345,
      "options": {
        "ignoreQueryString": {
          "enabled": true,
          "value": true
        }
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### Ignore all except

<p>In this sample, `ignore_query_string` is the option enabled above, so the request sets it to `enabled` false and keeps `value` true. `query_params_whitelist` names the parameters that stay in the cache key. Other parameters are ignored, so URLs that differ only in an unlisted parameter are cached as one object.</p>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Python SDK">
    ```python
    import os
    from gcore import Gcore

    client = Gcore()

    resource = client.cdn.cdn_resources.update(
        int(os.environ["CDN_RESOURCE_ID"]),
        options={
            "ignore_query_string": {"enabled": False, "value": True},
            "query_params_whitelist": {"enabled": True, "value": ["id"]},
        },
    )
    print(resource.options.query_params_whitelist.enabled, resource.options.query_params_whitelist.value)
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go SDK">
    ```go
    package main

    import (
        "context"
        "fmt"
        "os"
        "strconv"

        gcore "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go"
        "github.com/G-Core/gcore-go/cdn"
    )

    func main() {
        client := gcore.NewClient()
        ctx := context.Background()
        resourceID, err := strconv.ParseInt(os.Getenv("CDN_RESOURCE_ID"), 10, 64)
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }

        resource, err := client.CDN.CDNResources.Update(ctx, resourceID, cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParams{
            Options: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptions{
                IgnoreQueryString: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptionsIgnoreQueryString{
                    Enabled: false,
                    Value:   true,
                },
                QueryParamsWhitelist: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptionsQueryParamsWhitelist{
                    Enabled: true,
                    Value:   []string{"id"},
                },
            },
        })
        if err != nil {
            panic(err)
        }
        fmt.Println(resource.Options.QueryParamsWhitelist.Enabled, resource.Options.QueryParamsWhitelist.Value)
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="curl">
    ```bash
    curl -X PATCH "https://api.gcore.com/cdn/resources/$CDN_RESOURCE_ID" \
      -H "Authorization: APIKey $GCORE_API_KEY" \
      -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
      -d '{
        "options": {
          "ignoreQueryString": {
            "enabled": false,
            "value": true
          },
          "query_params_whitelist": {
            "enabled": true,
            "value": ["id"]
          }
        }
      }'
    ```

    <p>The API returns HTTP 200:</p>

    ```json
    {
      "id": 12345,
      "options": {
        "ignoreQueryString": {
          "enabled": false,
          "value": true
        },
        "query_params_whitelist": {
          "enabled": true,
          "value": ["id"]
        }
      }
    }
    ```
  </Tab>
</Tabs>

### Ignore only

<p>In this sample, `query_params_whitelist` is the option enabled above, so the request sets it to `enabled` false and keeps `id`. `query_params_blacklist` names the parameters left out of the cache key. Listed parameters are ignored, and every other parameter stays in the cache key.</p>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Python SDK">
    ```python

    from gcore import Gcore

    client = Gcore()

    resource = client.cdn.cdn_resources.update(
        int(os.environ["CDN_RESOURCE_ID"]),
        options={
            "query_params_whitelist": {"enabled": False, "value": ["id"]},
            "query_params_blacklist": {"enabled": True, "value": ["color"]},
        },
    )
    print(resource.options.query_params_blacklist.enabled, resource.options.query_params_blacklist.value)
    ```
  </Tab>

    ```go
            },
        })
    ```

    ```bash
      -d '{
        "options": {
          "query_params_whitelist": {
            "enabled": false,
    ```

    <p>The API returns HTTP 200:</p>

    ```json

      "id": 12345,
      "options": {
        "query_params_whitelist": {
          "enabled": false,
          "value": ["id"]
    ```

<p>Set `enabled` to false on the active option and keep `value`, so the full query string is part of the cache key again. The request below turns off Ignore only and keeps `color`.</p>

    ```python
        options={
            "query_params_blacklist": {"enabled": False, "value": ["color"]},
        },
    )
    print(resource.options.query_params_blacklist.enabled, resource.options.query_params_blacklist.value)
    ```
  </Tab>

    ```bash
        "options": {
    ```

    <p>The API returns HTTP 200:</p>

<Note>
In the Go SDK, set `Value` to true when `Enabled` is false for `ignoreQueryString` and `ignore_cookie`. Both fields set to false are omitted, and the stored option stays unchanged.
</Note>

## Set-Cookie

<p>Send `ignore_cookie` with `enabled` true and `value` true so files with different `Set-Cookie` header values are cached as one object. This option can stay enabled together with one query-string option.</p>

<Tabs>
  <Tab title="Python SDK">
    ```python
    import os
    from gcore import Gcore

    client = Gcore()

    resource = client.cdn.cdn_resources.update(
        int(os.environ["CDN_RESOURCE_ID"]),
        options={
            "ignore_cookie": {"enabled": True, "value": True},
        },
    )
    print(resource.options.ignore_cookie.enabled, resource.options.ignore_cookie.value)
    ```
  </Tab>
  <Tab title="Go SDK">

    ```go
        resource, err := client.CDN.CDNResources.Update(ctx, resourceID, cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParams{
            Options: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptions{
                IgnoreCookie: cdn.CDNResourceUpdateParamsOptionsIgnoreCookie{
                    Enabled: true,
                    Value:   true,
                },
            },
        })
        if err != nil {
    ```

    ```python
    resource = client.cdn.cdn_resources.update(
        int(os.environ["CDN_RESOURCE_ID"]),
        options={
            "ignore_cookie": {"enabled": False, "value": True},
        },
    )
    print(resource.options.ignore_cookie.enabled, resource.options.ignore_cookie.value)
    ```
  </Tab>

</MethodSection>
  <MethodSection id="terraform" label="Terraform">

<p>Control how query parameters and the `Set-Cookie` response header affect the CDN cache key with the [Terraform&nbsp;provider](/developer-tools/terraform/overview) v2. The cache key decides whether two URLs are stored as one object or as separate objects.</p>

<p>Enable only one of `ignore_query_string`, `query_params_whitelist`, and `query_params_blacklist`. A second enabled option returns HTTP 400. For `query_params_whitelist` and `query_params_blacklist`, an empty `value` list returns HTTP 400 while the option is enabled. An option left out of `options` stays unchanged, so set `enabled` to false on the active option in the same configuration and keep its `value`.</p>

<p>Enabling or changing a query-string option can invalidate cached URLs that contain a query string, so CDN servers request those files from the origin again and origin load can increase.</p>

## Query string

<p>`ignore_cookie` can stay enabled beside whichever query-string option is active. The configurations below switch modes in sequence. When a different query-string option is already enabled, set that option to `enabled` false in the same configuration and keep its `value`. Run `terraform apply` after editing `options`.</p>

### Ignore all

<p>Set `ignore_query_string` so URLs that differ only by query parameters are cached as one object.</p>

```hcl
resource "gcore_cdn_origin_group" "example" {
  name = "my-origin-group"

  sources = [
    {
      source  = "example.com"
      enabled = true
    }
  ]
}

resource "gcore_cdn_resource" "example" {
  cname           = "cdn.example.com"
  origin_group    = gcore_cdn_origin_group.example.id
  origin_protocol = "HTTPS"

  options = {
    ignore_query_string = {
      enabled = true
      value   = true
    }
  }
}
```

### Ignore all except

<p>Set `query_params_whitelist` to the parameter names that stay in the cache key. URLs that differ only by an unlisted parameter are cached as one object, while different values of a listed parameter are cached as separate objects. In this configuration, `ignore_query_string` is the option enabled above, so it is turned off and its stored `value` stays true. `id` stays in the cache key.</p>

```hcl
resource "gcore_cdn_origin_group" "example" {
  name = "my-origin-group"

  sources = [
    {
      source  = "example.com"
      enabled = true
    }
  ]
}

resource "gcore_cdn_resource" "example" {
  cname           = "cdn.example.com"
  origin_group    = gcore_cdn_origin_group.example.id
  origin_protocol = "HTTPS"

  options = {
    ignore_query_string = {
      enabled = false
      value   = true
    }
    query_params_whitelist = {
      enabled = true
      value   = ["id"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Ignore only

<p>Set `query_params_blacklist` to the parameter names left out of the cache key. Listed parameters are ignored, so URLs that differ only by those parameters are cached as one object, while every other parameter stays in the cache key. In this configuration, `query_params_whitelist` is the option enabled above, so it is turned off and `id` stays stored. `color` is ignored.</p>

```hcl
resource "gcore_cdn_origin_group" "example" {
  name = "my-origin-group"

  sources = [
    {
      source  = "example.com"
      enabled = true
    }
  ]
}

resource "gcore_cdn_resource" "example" {
  cname           = "cdn.example.com"
  origin_group    = gcore_cdn_origin_group.example.id
  origin_protocol = "HTTPS"

  options = {
    query_params_whitelist = {
      enabled = false
      value   = ["id"]
    }
    query_params_blacklist = {
      enabled = true
      value   = ["color"]
    }
  }
}
```

### Full query string

<p>Set `enabled` to false on the active option and keep `value`, so the full query string is part of the cache key again. This configuration turns off Ignore only and keeps `color`, while a disabled `query_params_whitelist` left out of `options` stays disabled and keeps `id`.</p>

```hcl
resource "gcore_cdn_origin_group" "example" {
  name = "my-origin-group"

  sources = [
    {
      source  = "example.com"
      enabled = true
    }
  ]
}

resource "gcore_cdn_resource" "example" {
  cname           = "cdn.example.com"
  origin_group    = gcore_cdn_origin_group.example.id
  origin_protocol = "HTTPS"

  options = {
    query_params_blacklist = {
      enabled = false
      value   = ["color"]
    }
  }
}
```

## Set-Cookie

<p>Set `ignore_cookie` so files with different `Set-Cookie` header values are cached as one object. A query-string option left out of `options` stays unchanged.</p>

```hcl
resource "gcore_cdn_origin_group" "example" {
  name = "my-origin-group"

  sources = [
    {
      source  = "example.com"
      enabled = true
    }
  ]
}

resource "gcore_cdn_resource" "example" {
  cname           = "cdn.example.com"
  origin_group    = gcore_cdn_origin_group.example.id
  origin_protocol = "HTTPS"

  options = {
    ignore_cookie = {
      enabled = true
      value   = true
    }
  }
}
```

### Set-Cookie with Ignore only

<p>Keep `ignore_cookie` enabled beside `query_params_blacklist`, so different `Set-Cookie` values are still one object and `color` stays out of the cache key. This configuration uses the query-string state from Ignore only, where `ignore_query_string` and `query_params_whitelist` are already disabled. When either is still enabled, set it to `enabled` false in the same configuration, because an omitted option stays unchanged.</p>

```hcl
resource "gcore_cdn_origin_group" "example" {
  name = "my-origin-group"

  sources = [
    {
      source  = "example.com"
      enabled = true
    }
  ]
}

resource "gcore_cdn_resource" "example" {
  cname           = "cdn.example.com"
  origin_group    = gcore_cdn_origin_group.example.id
  origin_protocol = "HTTPS"

  options = {
    query_params_blacklist = {
      enabled = true
      value   = ["color"]
    }
    ignore_cookie = {
      enabled = true
      value   = true
    }
  }
}
```

### Set-Cookie off

<p>Set `enabled` to false and keep `value` true. Files with different `Set-Cookie` header values are cached as separate objects again, and the stored `value` remains true.</p>

```hcl
resource "gcore_cdn_origin_group" "example" {
  name = "my-origin-group"

  sources = [
    {
      source  = "example.com"
      enabled = true
    }
  ]
}

resource "gcore_cdn_resource" "example" {
  cname           = "cdn.example.com"
  origin_group    = gcore_cdn_origin_group.example.id
  origin_protocol = "HTTPS"

  options = {
    ignore_cookie = {
      enabled = false
      value   = true
    }
  }
}
```
